current.text: Phoenix traded him to Charlotte in the Miles Bridges deal.
He is projected as Charlotte's sixth man. He moves into the starting lineup while Kon Knueppel is out.
Kon Knueppel is hurt and Coby White is out with a calf injury, so Charlotte is short on healthy players to start the season.
His role should be smaller than it was in Phoenix. He could still play about 27 minutes off the bench.
His shot volume should drop from last season's unusually high level, but his efficiency should improve. He should help as a secondary creator off the bench.

The experts disagree on his draft value. One ranks him around 100 to 115 (rounds 10 to 11) as a late-round swing, but says not to push his price much. Others would not draft him and see a low ceiling unless a starter like Brandon Miller misses games.
Charlotte plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
Charlotte plans to space the floor and take a lot of threes. Playmaking will be shared across several players.
Charlotte has a deep roster and projects as a play-in team.

durable.text: He can play shooting guard, small forward and power forward, and he can handle the ball.
He plays bigger than his size and drives downhill. He has had soft tissue problems.
Age and wear make him an injury risk. He has likely peaked and is entering the late part of his career.
Threes are his best category. His FG% is weak for his position, so he fits punt FG% builds.

note: Yahoo ranks him 177 and ESPN 158, and both value him near 0 USD, so in a 144-player draft he is a 1 USD last-round pick at most. Even the most positive expert call (100 to 115) comes with a warning not to push his price. He fits punt FG% builds that want threes, and his projected 2.7 threes per game are the reason to take him. Early in the season, check whether he starts while Knueppel and White are out, and whether his FG% gets back above the 40.3% he shot last season. If neither happens, he is a quick drop.
